source_text: Τοῦ ἐν ἁγίοις Πατρὸς ἡμῶν ΑΘΑΝΑΣΙΟΥ, ἀρχιεπισκόπου Ἀλεξανδρείας, πρὸς ΠΑΛΛΑΔΙΟΝ πρεσβύτερον ἐπιστολή. Ἀγαπητῷ υἱῷ Παλλαδίῳ πρεσβυτέρῳ Ἀθανάσιος ὁ ἐπίσκοπος, ἐν Κυρίῳ χαίρειν. Καὶ τὴν παρὰ σοῦ μόνου γραφεῖσαν ἐπιστολὴν δεξάμενος, ἐχάρην, μάλιστα ὅτι συνήθως ἔπνεες ὀρθοδοξίας. Καὶ τὴν αἰτίαν δὲ ἣν μετὰ τοῦ ἀγαπητοῦ ἡμῶν Ἰνοκεντίου διάγεις, οὐ πρῶτον νῦν, ἀλλ' ἔκπαλαι μαθὼν, ἀπεδεξάμην σου τὴν εὐλάβειαν. Οὕτω τοίνυν πράττων, γράφε καὶ γνώριζε ἡμῖν, πῶς ἐκεῖ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ, καὶ πῶς οἱ ἐχθροὶ τῆς ἀληθείας περὶ ἡμῶν διανοοῦνται. Ἐπειδὴ δὲ καὶ περὶ τῶν μοναζόντων τῶν ἐν Καισαρείᾳ ἐδήλωσας· ἔμαθον δὲ παρὰ τοῦ ἀγαπητοῦ ἡμῶν Διανίου, ὡς λυπουμένων καὶ ἀνθισταμένων αὐτῶν τῷ ἀγαπητῷ ἡμῶν Βασιλείῳ τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ· σὲ μὲν ἀπεδεξάμην δηλώσαντα, αὐτοῖς δὲ τὰ πρέποντα δεδήλωκα· ἵν' ὡς τέκνα ὑπακούωσι πατρὶ, καὶ μὴ ἀντιλέγωσιν, οἷς αὐτὸς δοκιμάζει. Εἰ μὲν γὰρ ὕποπτος ἦν περὶ τὴν ἀλήθειαν, καλῶς ἐμάχοντο· εἰ δὲ τεθαῤῥήκασι, τεθαῤῥήκαμεν δὲ καὶ πάντες ἡμεῖς, ὡς καύχημα τῆς Ἐκκλησίας ἐστὶν, ἀγωνιζόμενος μᾶλλον ὑπὲρ τῆς ἀληθείας, καὶ διδάσκων τοὺς δεομένους· οὐ χρὴ πρὸς τὸν τοιοῦτον μάχεσθαι, ἀλλὰ καὶ μᾶλλον ἀποδέχεσθαι τὴν ἀγαθὴν αὐτοῦ συνείδησιν. Ἐξ ὧν γὰρ διηγήσατο ὁ ἀγαπητὸς Διάνιος, μάτην φαίνονται λυπούμενοι. Αὐτὸς μὲν γὰρ, ὡς τεθάῤῥηκα, τοῖς ἀσθενοῦσιν ἀσθενὴς γίνεται, ἵνα τοὺς ἀσθενεῖς κερδήσῃ· οἱ δὲ ἀγαπητοὶ ἡμῶν, ἀποβλέποντες εἰς τὸν σκοπὸν τῆς ἀληθείας αὐτοῦ, καὶ τὴν οἰκονομίαν, δοξαζέτωσαν τὸν Κύριον, τὸν δεδωκότα τῇ Καππαδοκίᾳ τοιοῦτον ἐπίσκοπον, οἷον καὶ ἑκάστη χώρα ἔχειν εὔχεται. Καὶ σὺ οὖν, ἀγαπητὲ, θέλησον αὐτοῖς δηλῶσαι, ἵνα, ὡς ἔγραψα, πεισθῶσι. Τοῦτο γὰρ καὶ αὐτοὺς συνίστησιν εὐγνώμονας πρὸς πατέρα· τοῦτο καὶ τὴν εἰρήνην ταῖς Ἐκκλησίαις διαφυλάξει. Ἐῤῥῶσθαί σε ἐν Κυρίῳ εὔχομαι, ἀγαπητὲ υἱέ.
thought_title: Rejoicing at Palladius's orthodoxy and urging peace with Basil
orientation: Athanasius opens his letter to Palladius, rejoicing at his letter and orthodoxy, and then addresses the Caesarean monks' opposition to Bishop Basil.
pass_a_gloss: Of our Father among the saints ATHANASIUS, archbishop of Alexandria, to PALLADIUS the presbyter, a letter. To beloved son Palladius the presbyter, Athanasius the bishop, in the Lord greetings. And having received the letter written by you alone, I rejoiced, especially because as usual you were breathing orthodoxy. And the cause which you are conducting with our beloved Innocentius, not first now but long ago having learned, I accepted your piety. So then doing, write and make known to us, how there the brothers, and how the enemies of the truth are thinking about us. Since you also made clear about the monks in Caesarea; and I learned from our beloved Dianius, that they were grieving and resisting our beloved Basil the bishop; you I accepted for making clear, but to them I have made clear the fitting things; so that as children they obey a father, and do not speak against what he himself approves. For if he were suspect concerning the truth, they were fighting well; but if they have trusted, and we all have trusted, that he is a boast of the Church, contending rather for the truth, and teaching those in need; it is not necessary to fight against such a one, but rather to accept his good conscience. For from what beloved Dianius related, they appear to be grieving in vain. For he himself, as I have trusted, becomes weak to the weak, in order that he may gain the weak; but our beloved ones, looking to the goal of his truth, and the pastoral accommodation, let them glorify the Lord, who has given to Cappadocia such a bishop, such as each country prays to have. And you then, beloved, be willing to make clear to them, so that, as I wrote, they may be persuaded. For this both presents them as well-disposed toward a father; this also will preserve peace in the churches. I pray you to be strong in the Lord, beloved son.

choices.english: as usual you were breathing orthodoxy
choices.why: Keeps the imperfect 'ἔπνεες' as a past continuous action ('you were breathing') while 'συνήθως' conveys the habitual custom; 'breathing orthodoxy' preserves the metaphor and the glossary term 'orthodoxy'.
rejected: you breathe orthodoxy as is your custom

choices.why: The imperfect 'ἐμάχοντο' describes actual past fighting, not a hypothetical; 'well' renders 'καλῶς' as the manner of their fighting.
rejected: they would be right to fight

choices.why: The perfect 'τεθαῤῥήκασι' is about the monks' having placed confidence, not about Basil's quality; 'have trusted' preserves the perfect tense and the sense of shared confidence.
The perfect 'τεθάῤῥηκα' refers to Athanasius's having placed confidence, matching the earlier 'τεθαῤῥήκασι'; 'have trusted' keeps the perfect tense and the sense of shared confidence.
Uses the glossary English 'boast of the Church' for the fixed term.
Uses the glossary English 'pastoral accommodation' for Basil's management, avoiding the banned 'dispensation' or 'economy'.

bible_refs.note: τοῖς ἀσθενοῦσιν ἀσθενὴς γίνεται, ἵνα τοὺς ἀσθενεῖς κερδήσῃ

pass_b_english: From Athanasius, our father among the saints and archbishop of Alexandria, a letter to Palladius the presbyter. To my beloved son Palladius the presbyter, Athanasius the bishop: greetings in the Lord. I rejoiced when I received the letter written by you alone, especially because you were breathing orthodoxy as is your custom. And the cause you are engaged in with our beloved Innocentius—I learned of it not only now but long ago, and I accepted your piety. So as you continue in this way, write and let us know how the brothers there are doing, and how the enemies of the truth are thinking about us.

Since you also reported about the monks in Caesarea—and I learned from our beloved Dianius that they are grieved and resisting our beloved Basil the bishop—I approved you for reporting this, and I have written to them what is fitting: that as children they should obey their father and not speak against what he himself approves. For if he were suspect concerning the truth, they would be right to fight. But since they have confidence in him—and we all have confidence—that he is a boast of the Church, contending rather for the truth and teaching those in need, then it is not right to fight against such a man, but rather to accept his good conscience.

From what our beloved Dianius related, they appear to be grieved in vain. For he himself, as I am confident, becomes weak to the weak, so that he may gain the weak (1 Corinthians 9:22). But let our beloved ones, looking to his aim for the truth and his pastoral accommodation, glorify the Lord, who has given Cappadocia such a bishop as every region prays to have. And you then, beloved, be willing to make this known to them, so that, as I wrote, they may be persuaded. For this will show them to be well-disposed toward their father, and this will preserve peace in the churches. I pray that you fare well in the Lord, beloved son.

problems.why: Subject is Basil ('he has shown himself trustworthy'), not 'they have trusted'; English flips agency to monks trusting rather than Basil being trusted.
problems.ruling: τεθαῤῥήκασι is perf. pass. 'he has been trusted/shown trustworthy'; 'they have trusted' wrongly shifts subject to monks.

problems.why: English omits 'having reported/informed' (δηλώσαντα), losing the participial force: 'I approved you for having reported this.'
problems.fix: I approved you for reporting this
problems.ruling: σὲ ἀπεδεξάμην δηλώσαντα: 'I accepted you for reporting'; English 'your report' omits δηλώσαντα, losing Athanasius's commendation of Palladius's action.

edits.old: But if they have trusted—and all of us have trusted—that he is a boast of the Church
edits.new: But if he has proved trustworthy—and all of us have trusted—that he is a boast of the Church

edits.old: I accepted your report, and I have written to them what is fitting
edits.new: I approved you for reporting this, and I have written to them what is fitting

fixed: Changed 'if they have trusted' to 'if he has proved trustworthy' because the Greek τεθαῤῥήκασι refers to Basil being trusted, not the monks trusting.
Changed 'I accepted your report' to 'I approved you for reporting this' to include the participial force of δηλώσαντα.

problems.quote: if he has proved trustworthy—and all of us have trusted
problems.source_quote: εἰ δὲ τεθαῤῥήκασι, τεθαῤῥήκαμεν δὲ καὶ πάντες ἡμεῖς
problems.why: τεθαῤῥήκασι refers to the monks having confidence/trusted, not Basil having 'proved trustworthy'; the construction is 'if they have trusted [him]—and we all have trusted [him too]'.
problems.fix: if they have trusted him—and we all have trusted him

problems.why: Same verb: means 'as I have trusted/confided,' not 'as I have trusted [in him]' in the sense of believing him reliable; it's about Athanasius's confidence in Basil's conduct.
τῆς ἀληθείας is objective genitive: 'the goal [aimed at] by his truth' or 'the goal of [i.e., aimed at by] truth'—not 'his truth' as possessive.
problems.fix: the goal aimed at by his truth
problems.ruling: αὐτοῦ likely refers to Basil, not truth; 'his truth' misreads genitive, misleading reader.

edits.old: if he has proved trustworthy—and all of us have trusted—that he is a boast of the Church
edits.new: if they have trusted him—and we all have trusted him—that he is a boast of the Church

edits.old: as I have trusted, becomes weak to the weak
edits.new: as I am confident, becomes weak to the weak

edits.old: the goal of his truth and his pastoral accommodation
edits.new: the goal aimed at by his truth and his pastoral accommodation

fixed: Changed 'if he has proved trustworthy—and all of us have trusted' to 'if they have trusted him—and we all have trusted him' because τεθαῤῥήκασι refers to the monks' trust, not Basil's trustworthiness.
Changed 'as I have trusted' to 'as I am confident' because τεθάρρηκα expresses Athanasius's confidence in Basil's conduct, not trust in his reliability.
Changed 'the goal of his truth' to 'the goal aimed at by his truth' because τῆς ἀληθείας is an objective genitive, not possessive.

problems.quote: if they have trusted him—and we all have trusted him
problems.source_quote: εἰ δὲ τεθαῤῥήκασι, τεθαῤῥήκαμεν δὲ καὶ πάντες ἡμεῖς
problems.why: The Greek is causal/declarative ('since they have confidence, and we all have confidence'), not conditional; this changes Athanasius's certainty to speculation.
problems.fix: since they have confidence in him—and we all have confidence
problems.ruling: εἰ δέ after εἰ μὲν...ἐμάχοντο is conditional 'but if'; rendering 'if...have trusted' is correct, not causal 'since'.

problems.quote: the goal aimed at by his truth
problems.why: τῆς ἀληθείας αὐτοῦ is objective genitive: 'the goal of [i.e. aimed at] the truth', not 'his truth'; the truth is the object, not possessed by Basil.
problems.ruling: τῆς ἀληθείας αὐτοῦ: αὐτοῦ refers to Basil, making 'his truth' possessive. Genitive likely modifies σκοπόν, not truth itself.

edits.old: But if they have trusted him—and we all have trusted him—that he is a boast of the Church
edits.new: But since they have confidence in him—and we all have confidence—that he is a boast of the Church

edits.old: the goal aimed at by his truth and his pastoral accommodation
edits.new: the goal of the truth and his pastoral accommodation

fixed: Changed conditional to causal: 'εἰ δὲ τεθαῤῥήκασι, τεθαῤῥήκαμεν δὲ καὶ πάντες ἡμεῖς' is declarative confidence, not a condition.
Changed 'the goal aimed at by his truth' to 'the goal of the truth': 'τῆς ἀληθείας αὐτοῦ' is objective genitive, the truth is the goal's object, not Basil's possession.

fixed.fix: they would be right to fight
fixed.note: εἰ…ἦν…ἐμάχοντο is a contrary-to-fact condition, and "they were fighting well" reads as a real past event, which breaks the logic.
αὐτοῦ makes the aim Basil's, and the English drops the possessive so the goal seems to belong to the truth itself.

dismissed.why: The Greek means 'as he is confident' (Basil), not 'as I am confident' (Athanasius).
dismissed.note: τεθάῤῥηκα is first person singular, so "as I am confident" is correct.
